title: Up and Running with Rapidus : How Japan and Cutting-Edge Technologies are Transforming Semiconductor Manufacturing
problem: Japan's semiconductor manufacturing capacity has declined; existing fabs use older process technologies limiting competitiveness in advanced node production.
motivation: National and regional semiconductor self-sufficiency drives demand for new leading-edge manufacturing capacity independent of Taiwan/Korea.
method: Rapidus is a government-backed Japanese semiconductor factory that combines cutting-edge manufacturing techniques to produce advanced chips. It uses extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography—a technology for etching extremely fine details onto silicon—along with advanced packaging that densely connects chip components. The factory controls more of its own manufacturing chain rather than outsourcing, and focuses on gradually increasing production while optimizing how many chips work correctly (yield).
key_novelty: A government-backed Japanese fab integrates extreme ultraviolet lithography and advanced packaging technologies to manufacture semiconductors at advanced nodes.
contributions: Advanced node fabrication facility in Japan
EUV lithography integration for sub-7nm processes
Novel packaging and chiplet integration strategies
limitations: Specific technical details on process nodes, yield rates, and timeline not in abstract.
